data.title: Micron stock continues slump, analysts are saying it's a buying opportunity
data.description:
Micron Technology shares MU fell about 4% on Friday, taking the weekly decline to 10% as investors assessed the potential threat from China’s memory-chip industry and concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom.

The stock has retreated from its summer peak of more than $1,200, despite having more than tripled this year.

The recent sell-off followed progress reported by Chinese memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) on a denser dynamic random access memory (DRAM) architecture known as 4F-squared.

The design could allow manufacturers to fit more memory cells into a smaller area, potentially improving production economics.

CXMT has also indicated plans to introduce server-memory products using the technology by the end of 2026, prompting concerns that Chinese suppliers could eventually expand their presence in the market.

However, analysts argue that the development does not necessarily threaten Micron’s position in high-bandwidth memory (HBM), a specialised technology used in AI servers.

CXMT’s breakthrough raises concerns about competition

Micron and South Korea’s SK Hynix both fell sharply after CXMT’s announcement.

By Friday, October 16, Micron had lost around 10% for the week, while SK Hynix was down nearly 15%.

The market reaction reflects concerns that advances in Chinese memory manufacturing could increase supply and put pressure on prices.

However, progress in chip design does not automatically translate into competitive mass production.

Citi analysts said CXMT’s manufacturing process remained several generations behind industry leaders.

They estimated that mass production using the new architecture was unlikely before 2028, potentially giving Micron and SK Hynix time to advance their own technologies.

The possibility of additional supply remains a concern, particularly if Chinese manufacturers eventually expand production enough to affect industry pricing.

Analysts see limited immediate threat to AI memory demand

Fundstrat vice president for market intelligence Kent Fung said CXMT’s new architecture could challenge conventional server DRAM but did not directly compete with the HBM products required for AI servers.

“Investors should consider the possibility that the knee-jerk response to CXMT’s announcement has been a bit of an overreaction,” Fung wrote in a research note on Thursday.

He added that CXMT’s breakthrough had a weaker connection to AI and therefore potentially weaker implications for memory and storage stocks’ growth prospects.

The distinction matters because conventional DRAM serves computers and servers more broadly, while HBM is designed to move data rapidly to AI processors.

CXMT’s progress in conventional memory does not establish that it can immediately challenge the advanced HBM products supplied by Micron and SK Hynix.

Micron’s fiscal 2026 annual report also said AI-driven memory demand was outpacing industry supply, supporting stronger pricing and margins.

Rising memory prices support Micron’s investment case

KeyBanc analyst John Vinh reiterated a $1,750 price target on Micron and described it as one of his favourite investment ideas following a trip to assess Asian supply chains.

Vinh said DRAM prices in the fourth quarter were expected to rise by 15% to 20% from the previous quarter. He also noted that Google was considering extending long-term memory-supply agreements through 2035.

While Vinh said he did not expect the current memory upcycle to last until 2031 or 2035, he argued that the potential agreements suggested customers were concerned about shortages persisting beyond 2028.

These expectations offer support for Micron’s outlook, although the potential for increased competition remains a risk.

If Chinese suppliers add meaningful capacity, additional supply could weaken memory prices and reduce the returns earned on new factories.

Even without an immediate loss of AI customers, investors could become less willing to pay premium valuations for earnings that may be unusually strong near the peak of a memory-chip cycle.

The outlook therefore depends not only on AI demand but also on how quickly supply expands and how that affects pricing.

data.title: Dow opens 240 pts higher as AI stocks slide and inflation concerns weigh
data.description:
US stocks opened mixed on Friday as renewed selling in technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks weighed on sentiment, while gains in Tesla offered some support.

Investors also assessed persistent inflation pressures and the outlook for Federal Reserve interest rates ahead of the central bank’s October policy meeting.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 242 points while the S&P 500 gained 0.11%. The Nasdaq composite fell 0.28%.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were on track for weekly losses, while the Dow remained positioned for a weekly advance.

Tesla rises as AI stocks face renewed selling

Tesla shares climbed around 0.8% in trading after the electric vehicle maker unveiled its redesigned Roadster, developed in collaboration with SpaceX and featuring rocket-style thrusters.

The vehicle is not expected to enter production until 2028.

SpaceX shares fell 2.5%.

Gains in Tesla contrasted with continued weakness across several AI-related stocks.

Nvidia-backed data centre operator CoreWeave fell 6.6% in trading, reversing some of Thursday’s rebound, as concerns about its debt burden persisted.

The company’s bonds sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.

Other neocloud companies, including Nebius Group and Iren, declined more than 5% each. Micron Technology shares fell 3.6%, while Intel dropped 2.18%.

Semiconductor stocks have also faced pressure amid concerns about growing Chinese competition in the memory chip market.

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF fell 1.7% in trading and was down 8.9% for the week.

The declines reflect investor concerns that data centre operators may struggle to generate profits quickly enough to service their debt, particularly if borrowing costs rise.

David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, said the pullback in memory chip stocks and concerns over CoreWeave’s debt had given investors a reason to reduce exposure to companies linked to AI.

“There’s still some caution out there,” Morrison said.

"Just a touch of profit-taking after yesterday’s rebound, or something more serious? Time will tell. But it could be argued that investor behaviour since the middle of this week could provide some insight into the future.", he added.

Inflation and Fed outlook weigh on sentiment

Investors also remained focused on hotter-than-expected inflation data released this week.

US consumer and producer prices have shown persistent pressure, with wholesale inflation recording its biggest increase since 2022 and consumer inflation remaining above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target.

Elevated energy prices following the US-Iran war have added to inflation concerns, complicating the outlook for monetary policy.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking at an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok, said the US economy remained resilient and was benefiting from an AI-driven investment boom.

He also noted that stronger spending was contributing to inflation, without offering a clear signal on the Fed’s next policy decision.

Markets increasingly expect the central bank to leave interest rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting. The CME Group’s FedWatch tool indicated an 85% probability of a hold.

Morrison also pointed to sharp movements in Treasury yields as a potential signal of changing investor sentiment.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.30% on Wednesday before falling to a three-week low on Thursday.

He said the moves could reflect concerns about a possible unwinding of the AI trade or a shift towards safer assets.

Netflix and other stocks move in trading

Among other individual stocks, Varonis Systems gained 2.7% after Thoma Bravo-owned Proofpoint agreed to acquire the data security company in an all-cash deal valued at $6.3 billion.

Netflix shares declined 1.7% after the streaming company appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer, replacing Bela Bajaria.

Meanwhile, concerns about AI financing costs also extended to private companies.

Reuters reported that some current and prospective investors in Anthropic’s planned initial public offering were considering a lower valuation amid worries about rising AI funding costs.

data.title: Netflix stock falls 3% as content shake-up fails to ease investor worries
data.description:
Netflix shares NFLX fell 3.5% in premarket trading on Friday after the streaming company announced a leadership change aimed at strengthening its film and television programming amid slowing viewer engagement and increased competition.

The company said former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice would become its chief content officer on October 26, replacing Bela Bajaria, who is leaving after nearly a decade at Netflix.

The announcement came a day after the company revealed plans to cut approximately 6% of its workforce, or around 1,000 jobs.

Netflix shares had already declined 23% this year through Thursday's close, as concerns about its share of television viewing and ability to produce popular content weighed on investor sentiment.

Netflix replaces Bela Bajaria with Peter Rice

Rice will oversee Netflix's film and television slate, as well as live events, taking responsibility for a broad range of programming as the company seeks to improve viewer engagement.

He previously managed Disney's television operations, including ABC, FX, Hulu and its television studios.

Before joining Disney, Rice held senior positions at 21st Century Fox and Fox Searchlight Pictures.

During his tenure at Disney, the company released critically acclaimed programmes such as Modern Family and Abbott Elementary and approved projects including The Bear.

Netflix co-chief executive Ted Sarandos praised Rice's industry experience and relationships with Hollywood talent, describing him as one of the entertainment industry's most effective large-scale operators.

Sarandos also thanked Bajaria for helping expand Netflix's programming into unscripted shows, live events and sports.

Bajaria had overseen the company's global film and television slate since 2023.

The leadership change comes as Netflix explores new programming formats, including video podcasts and live sports, to compete for audiences against platforms such as YouTube and TikTok.

Viewer engagement and competition weigh on shares

Netflix has faced concerns that its share of television viewing hours is declining, raising questions about whether slowing engagement could eventually affect subscriber growth.

The company has struggled to produce cultural hits on the scale of earlier successes such as Stranger Things and Wednesday.

Finding another globally popular programme could help restore momentum, although the performance of future releases remains uncertain.

Sarandos acknowledged the challenge at a conference last month, saying: “Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster.”

Netflix also drew scrutiny in July when it announced that it would publish its engagement report once a year instead of twice a year, starting in 2027.

Competition for viewers has intensified as established streaming services and digital platforms vie for audiences' time.

The company had also sought to expand its programming library through a potential acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, but Paramount, now called Skydance, ultimately won the bidding contest.

Job cuts and upcoming earnings in focus

The appointment of Rice follows Netflix's announcement that it would eliminate around 1,000 positions, marking its largest round of layoffs in at least four years.

The combination of job cuts and a leadership transition highlights the pressure on the company to improve operating efficiency while strengthening its content offering.

Rice's priorities will include Netflix's film and television productions and live events.

Industry insiders are also watching for his decisions on key leadership roles and the performance of major upcoming projects, including La Bola Negra and Narnia, which are associated with current film chair Dan Lin.

Netflix is scheduled to report earnings on Tuesday, giving investors an opportunity to assess its latest financial performance and management's outlook.

The company's ability to improve viewer engagement and deliver successful programming will remain central to its efforts to rebuild investor confidence and reverse its share-price decline.

Wedbush reiterated its buy position on the stock while cutting the target price from $105 to $90.

BMO Capital also maintained its buy position and slashed the target price from $135 to $125.

data.title: Zeta Global stock is soaring: Here is why and what comes next
data.description:
Zeta Global stock continued its strong rally, reaching its highest level since November 2024, and is slowly nearing its record high of $38.15. It has jumped by over 230% from its 2025 lows, with the market capitalization hitting $8.42 billion. This rally may continue after Goldman Sachs upgraded its target.

Goldman Sachs has upgraded Zeta Global stock target

Zeta Global is a top company in the advertising industry, where it uses artificial intelligence, customer data analytics, and digital marketing automation solutions to help clients. It works with large firms across most sectors to help them find new customers, predict what they are likely to buy, and then deliver personalized advertisements.

Goldman Sachs analysts believe that Zeta Global has more room for growth. They upgraded the company from neutral to buy, with the price target being $45, which is about 35% above the current level. The analysts pointed to its strong demand and revenues, and the need for personalized marketing. 

Other analysts have been relatively bullish on the stock. Roth Capital has set a target of $55, while New Street Research, KeyCorp, Truist Financial, and DA Davidson have a target of $38. The average target among analysts is $36, where it is trading at today.

Zeta growth to continue

The most recent financial showed that its revenue rose by 44% in the second quarter to $443 million. Its adjusted EBITDA soared by 56% to $92 million, while its adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 20.7%.

Notably, this report was the 20th straight “beat and raise” quarter. It predicted that it is on track to hit its 2028 EBITDA and free cash flow targets. Its annual revenue is expected to jump to $2.3 billion in 2028 from $1.8 billion this year.

The adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to move to 25%. If this is correct, the figure will jump to $573 million from $405 million this year, with its free cash flow target hitting $371 million.

These numbers may help to justify its substantial valuation. It trades with a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 35, much higher than the forward S&P 500’s 19.1. 

On the positive side, the company has a forward PEG ratio of 1.04, slightly lower than the sector median of 1.17. Its Rule-of-40 multiple also stands at 100. 

Zeta Global shares technical analysis

Zeta shares chart | Source: TradingView

The weekly chart shows that Zeta Global shares have continued soaring in the past few months. It jumped from $10.6 in 2025 to a high of $35.6 as the rally gained momentum. 

The stock is in the process of forming a cup-and-handle pattern whose upper side is at $38.15, its highest point in 2024. This pattern often leads to more upside over time. 

Zeta has remained above the 50-week moving average. Therefore, the stock will likely continue rising, with the next target to watch being at $50. This view will be confirmed if it moves above the all-time high of $38.15.

data.title: Top FTSE 100 shares to watch: Barclays, Unilever, Persimmon, Aberdeen Group
data.description:
The FTSE 100 has rallied strongly over the past few weeks, climbing from a low of 10,370 earlier this month to around 10,820. That momentum will be in focus next week as investors turn their attention to key UK economic data and earnings reports from major companies.

UK to publish important macro data

The FTSE 100 will react to some important numbers from the UK. The Office of National Statistics (ONS) will publish the latest jobs numbers on Tuesday. After that, the agency will release the September consumer inflation data on Wednesday. 

Economists expect the data to show that the headline and core CPI jumped in September as energy prices soared. Finally, the UK will release the official retail sales report, which are expected to show that volume rose in September. 

These numbers will help the Bank of England (BoE) when delivering its interest rate decision later this month. Economists expect the bank to hike interest rates later this month.

Barclays stock in focus as it releases earnings

BARC stock has been under pressure in the past few months as concerns about the investment banking division rose. After starting the year well, there are signs that the trend is getting worse, with the volume of deals falling by over 40% sequentially in the third quarter.

The severity of this issue was seen this week when US banks like Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Bank of America. Morgan Stanley’s investment banking revenue rose by just 2% to $2.16 billion, $110 million lower than expected. 

Analysts expect that Barclays UK will have a profit before tax of 931 million pounds, with its UK corporate bank making 291 million pounds. Its private bank and wealth management division is expected to make 99 million pounds.

Unilever

Unilever stock has staged a strong comeback in the past few months. It has jumped from a low of 4,000p earlier this year to the current 4,885p. This rally will be in the spotlight as investors react to its upcoming earnings report.

These results will provide hints on how the company is doing. The last earnings report showed that its sales growth rose 4.8% in the second quarter, with its turnover soaring to over 25.6 billion euros. Most of this growth came from its home care business, followed by its beauty and wellbeing segment. 

Analysts expect the upcoming report to show that its underlying sales growth rose 4.8% in the third quarter. Its volume is expected to rise 2.5%, while its price soared by 2.3%.

Persimmon

Persimmon stock has been highly volatile in the past few weeks. It surged on September 28 after the UK announced a new program to help consumers buy homes. It hit a high of 1,340p and then pulled back as the momentum faded. 

The upcoming earnings report will likely show that its business deteriorated in the third quarter because of the elevated mortgage rates. Housebuilders are also facing the challenge of high cost of doing business as inflation rises. 

The most recent results showed that its profit before tax rose by 3% to 170 million pounds in the first half of the year. This happened as the number of house completions rose by 7%, while the average asking price rose by just 3%.

Aberdeen Group

Aberdeen Group, formerly known as Abrdn, has stayed inside a narrow range in the past few months. It has remained between the support and resistance levels of 231p and 255p since July. 

The company will react to the upcoming earnings on October 21. Its last earnings report showed that its net operating revenue rose 2% to 643 million pounds. Similarly, the profit before tax rose 2% to 276 million pounds, with its assets under management hitting 576 billion pounds.

These results will provide more hints on its business and whether its revenue and assets under management continued to grow.

data.title: Strategy stock analysis as Bitcoin price rally and ETF inflows loses momentum
data.description:
Strategy stock retreated more than 5% on Friday as its recent momentum faded. The shares fell to $136, which is 20% below their September high and their lowest level since September 18. The pullback may continue as Bitcoin loses traction and dilution concerns gain steam.

Strategy stock falls as Bitcoin loses traction

MSTR stock dropped as the recent Bitcoin rally lost traction. After peaking at $87,270 in September, it dropped to the current $80,980 as demand in the futures and ETF market waned. 

Spot Bitcoin ETFs have had over $534 million in outflows this month, a big reversal from the $2.6 billion inflows experienced in September and the $3.52 billion they added in August. In total, these funds have had cumulative inflows of $56.9 billion, with BlackRock’s IBIT having $66 billion in assets. 

Bitcoin’s futures open interest has also dropped modestly in the past few days. These inflows dropped to $52 billion from last month’s high of $62 billion. Falling open interest is a sign that demand among speculative investors is fading. The Coinbase Bitcoin Premium Index has remained in the red since September 26. 

Strategy is usually affected by Bitcoin’s price action because of its vast holdings. It holds 848,250 coins currently valued at $68.6 billion. 

For investors, there are signs that the company will continue to dilute its investors since it uses its stock to buy Bitcoin. Its outstanding shares have jumped to 352 million from 93.2 million in 2022.

Bitcoin price may drop further this year

Technicals suggest that BTC price has dropped in the past few weeks, moving from $87,270 late September to the current $80,890. It formed a double-top pattern and a neckline at $82,300. This pattern often leads to a strong bearish breakout.

The coin has moved below the important support level of $82,233, its highest level on May 10 this year. At the same time, it has moved below the 50-day moving average, while the Relative Strength Index (RSI) has continued falling. 

These technicals suggest that the coin may drop further towards the support of $74,933, its lowest level in September. Such a move would bring the value of Strategy’s coins to $63.4 billion.

BTC price chart | Source: TradingView

MSTR stock price technical analysis

The daily chart shows that Strategy peaked at $171.40 on September 22 and is currently at $134. This retreat has coincided with the ongoing Bitcoin sell-off. 

Strategy has already dropped below the 25-day moving average and the descending trendline that links the highest point in May, September, and October. 

The two lines of the MACD indicator have made a bearish crossover and are pointing downwards. Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the psychological level of $100. 

The bearish outlook will be invalidated if Strategy jumps above the resistance level of $150. A move above that level will point to more gains, potentially to $200. 

MSTR stock chart | Source: TradingView

Analysts have maintained a bullish outlook for MSTR. For example, Cantor Fitzgerald has placed a target of $208, while Citigroup has a target of $240. Bernstein believes that the stock will jump to $350, while B.Riley sees it rising to $195.

data.title: Why is Moderna down 10% on Friday?
data.description:
Moderna MRNA shares suffered a sharp reversal on Friday, falling close to 10% after a strong October rally had pushed the biotechnology to its 52-week high.

The shares, which reached $242.29 during their recent advance, were trading near $213 at the time of writing. The decline erased a significant portion of this month's gains, which had exceeded 25% before Friday's session.

Despite the latest retreat, Moderna has been one of the market's strongest performers over the past 12 months, with its stock rising close to 700%. Progress in the company's cancer treatment research has helped fuel investor enthusiasm, but the rapid appreciation has also put its valuation under greater scrutiny.

Analyst targets lag behind the share price

The sell-off mimicked a negative trading day for the broader market. Moderna's peers recorded more modest moves, with Pfizer gaining 0.42% while BioNTech fell around 2.5%.

The sharp difference in performance suggests that Moderna faced company-specific selling pressure rather than simply following the wider biotechnology sector lower. Profit booking can be explained as one of the reasons but there were other catalysts as well.

One factor drawing attention was Goldman Sachs' latest assessment of the stock. The investment bank increased its price target to $137 from $120 but kept its Neutral rating unchanged.

With Moderna trading around $212, Goldman's revised valuation remains considerably below the prevailing share price. The change therefore offered limited support for investors looking for further confirmation that the recent rally could continue.

The cautious stance follows Citigroup's decision to downgrade Moderna to Sell recently. Together, the analyst views highlight a growing divide between the market's enthusiasm for the company's progress and the valuations.

Cancer treatment remains central to the investment story

Much of the interest in Moderna has centred on its efforts to expand beyond vaccines into cancer treatment. The stock had dipped sharply post COVID-19 but has witnessed a dramatic turnaround since last year.

In August, the company reported positive Phase 3 results for its personalized cancer vaccine, strengthening expectations that the treatment could become an important part of its future business.

The therapy, intismeran autogene, is being developed in partnership with Merck. Investors are now awaiting more detailed findings from the late-stage trial to assess the treatment's potential more closely.

The upcoming data could help clarify whether the clinical progress that has helped drive Moderna's stock higher can translate into a commercially significant treatment.

For investors, however, the timing creates a difficult balance. Expectations surrounding the cancer vaccine have contributed to the stock's substantial gains, leaving the market to judge how much potential success is already reflected in the share price.

Can the rally regain momentum?

Friday's decline illustrates the pressure that can emerge when a stock advances rapidly ahead of further evidence to support its valuation.

Moderna's progress in cancer treatment has reshaped investor expectations, but analysts' price targets suggest that confidence in the science does not necessarily translate into agreement about the stock's current worth.

The next detailed results for intismeran autogene will be an important point of focus as investors evaluate the treatment's prospects and Moderna's longer-term growth potential.

data.title: Prediction Markets are betting on a Tesla, SpaceX merger in 2027
data.description:
Traders are increasingly betting that billionaire Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX will merge by early 2027, bringing fresh momentum to one of Wall Street’s most ambitious merger theories.

By Friday morning, prediction-market odds of a merger before March had reached 56%, compared with 29% only earlier this week.

The data follows a Barclays’ research note outlining the strategic rationale for a combination.

Why a Tesla-SpaceX merger is gaining credibility

Barclays’ senior analyst Dan Levy sees a possible announcement before Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting, which his team expects to take place no later than December 6.

That creates two distinct timelines: a potential announcement in 2026 and prediction-market bets extending into 2027. Neither establishes when a transaction would actually close.

The investment case centres on artificial intelligence (AI).

Tesla is developing machines that operate in the physical world, including robotaxis and Optimus humanoid robots.

SpaceX’s AI businesses could supply complementary software and computing capabilities.

Barclays argues that bringing these together could accelerate development across both companies.

In practical terms, the proposed advantage will be tighter coordination between teams developing intelligent software and those building products that use it.

Here’s what the two companies would gain

Terafab offers a more concrete explanation for the merger discussion.

Barclays identifies the semiconductor initiative involving “Tesla, SpaceX and xAI” as a potential catalyst, because managing a shared project across separate companies creates governance and approval complexity.

A combination could simplify those decisions and align investment priorities.

For Tesla, the benefits include “closer integration” with AI software and satellite connectivity.

For SpaceX, Tesla’s energy products and production capabilities could complement its infrastructure ambitions.

Reported possibilities include “Grok-enabled” interactions for Optimus, Starlink connectivity for vehicles, and Tesla energy systems supporting SpaceX data centres.

The economic question is whether common ownership would make those projects faster or cheaper than existing commercial partnerships.

Combining businesses only creates shareholder value if the resulting gains justify the acquisition terms, integration costs and additional complexity.

Deal terms will matter more than betting odds

Investors still lack the information needed to judge an actual transaction.

Barclays has explored an all-stock structure in which SpaceX acquires Tesla, but that remains an analyst’s projection only for now.  

For shareholders, the eventual terms would determine how much of the combined business they own and which investment risks they inherit.

Governance would also deserve scrutiny because both companies are led by Musk.

A compelling AI narrative cannot settle those questions. Investors would need formal disclosures explaining valuation, financing, voting rights, and the approval process before assessing whether a merger benefits them.

Note that Wall Street currently rates both of Musk’s companies, SpaceX and Tesla, at Overweight – with mean price targets signaling significant upside potential from here.

data.title: Apple shares rise after iPhone Duo pre-orders sell out within minutes
data.description:
Apple AAPL shares edged higher after the company's first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, sold out shortly after preorders opened on Friday.

At 11:05 AM EST, the stock was trading around $346.46, up approximately 1.3% from Thursday's close, as investors assessed the initial response to Apple's long-awaited entry into the foldable phone segment.

Users on social media reported that estimated delivery dates for the new device had shifted from October 23 to late January, suggesting that initial demand was running ahead of available supply.

Sentiments were also helped by other company-specific developments.

iPhone Duo marks Apple's entry into foldables

Apple has entered the foldable smartphone market after lagging behind Samsung and Chinese manufacturers in the category.

The passport-sized iPhone Duo features a 5.4-inch front display and a 7.6-inch foldable internal screen. Apple expects foldable smartphones to account for roughly 10% of the market by 2029.

The initial response to the device could help the company establish a foothold in the segment, although preorder demand alone does not determine the product's eventual sales performance.

The launch also comes as Apple seeks to diversify its growth drivers beyond its established iPhone lineup.

The reported weakness in demand for the iPhone 18 Pro models had raised concerns about the outlook for its premium smartphones, making the reception of the foldable device an important development for investors.

Apple Intelligence clears regulatory hurdle in China

In another development, Apple Chairman Tim Cook announced during a visit to Shanghai that Apple Intelligence had received regulatory clearance from Chinese authorities.

The software is expected to begin rolling out to users in China as a test version later in October. Planned features include writing assistance, photo cleanup, and live translation.

To comply with local requirements, Apple has partnered with Chinese e-commerce company Alibaba to use its Qwen AI models for users in mainland China.

Apple and Meta collaborate

Apple is also collaborating with Meta to optimize the latter's new Muse Spark Open AI model for Apple's high-end Mac computers.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg publicly thanked Apple's engineering team for helping optimize the model to run on M5 Ultra Mac computers.

The collaboration focuses on enabling Meta's large open-weight AI model to run locally on Apple's high-end Mac Studio desktop systems.

The partnership signals a potential shift in the relationship between the companies, which have previously clashed over issues including data privacy and App Store fees.

Under Apple CEO John Ternus and Meta CEO Zuckerberg, the work brings the two technology companies together on AI infrastructure and model performance.

Analysts largely bullish but demand concerns weigh

Analysts remain bullish over Apple's stock prospects, but there are some concerns as well.

UBS maintained its Neutral rating on Apple with a $296 price target, pointing to iPhone availability data showing shorter waiting times than a year earlier.

The firm viewed the decline in wait times, alongside a stable supply backdrop, as a concern for the iPhone maker.

KeyBanc also maintained an Underweight rating on the stock, reflecting a more cautious outlook.

JP Morgan, however, said the reported reductions in iPhone 18 Pro production orders were consistent with the adjustments Apple typically makes each year.

data.title: CoreWeave stock drops nearly 20% this week. Why analysts say its a buy
data.description:
CoreWeave stock CRWV fell again on Friday after recovering in the previous session, putting the AI cloud computing company on track for a steep weekly loss as investors continued to worry about its debt-financed expansion amid rising borrowing costs.

The stock dropped about 7.2% on Friday, even as the S&P 500 edged higher.

Nasdaq Composite opened lower by about 0.4%.

CoreWeave shares have lost nearly 20% this week as concerns over inflation, interest rates and the financing requirements of artificial intelligence infrastructure weighed on sentiment.

In addition, Gartner released research indicating that by 2030, 80% of neocloud providers will most likely cease independent operations.

Rising borrowing costs put debt under scrutiny

For some analysts, CoreWeave has become a symbol of the debt-fuelled AI infrastructure boom, in which companies are committing billions of dollars to data centres and computing capacity before the long-term returns on that investment are fully established.

The sell-off intensified after hotter-than-expected US inflation data on Wednesday heightened concerns that interest rates could remain elevated, increasing the cost of financing capital-intensive AI infrastructure.

Nicholas Mugalli, chief investment officer at World Trade Securities, said CoreWeave short sellers made around $806 million in paper profit on Wednesday when the stock fell 15.5%.

CoreWeave's $2.8 billion of 9.75% bonds issued in April traded at 79.5 cents on the dollar on Thursday, yielding more than 15%, according to data provided by BondCliQ.

The loss-making cloud computing company has about $50 billion in debt.

"A hot inflation print triggered a ​sharp selloff in CoreWeave because its business model is a highly indebted play on future data center demand," BCA Research analysts said.

"Although the rest ​of the tech complex is also sensitive to the ​pace and magnitude of AI adoption and use, it is, on average, ‌considerably ⁠less sensitive to interest rates"

CoreWeave rents out Nvidia graphics processing units and supplies computing power to AI laboratories such as OpenAI and major technology companies including Meta Platforms.

It operates data centres across the US and internationally.

The business depends on continued demand for computing capacity, while its expansion requires substantial upfront investment.

That combination has left investors weighing the strength of its contracted revenue against the risks associated with its debt and future capital expenditure.

Why neoclouds face a threat, but CoreWeave is likely to survive

Gartner said in 2026, AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure, and are forecast to invest an additional $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030, but enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures during this period.

A cumulative $8.5 trillion in revenue would be required to recover the massive AI spend, according to Gartner; however, total enterprise and consumer AI revenue that can be attributed to AI data centers during this period is forecast to reach no more than $3.6 trillion, it said.

"Failure to achieve sustainable ROIC on rapidly depreciating assets would almost certainly necessitate write-downs," it said.

Neoclouds will be among the most exposed to the imbalance between revenue and capital spending, and cost pressure and a lack of a differentiating business model will force over 80% of neocloud providers to cease independent operations, it said.

Melvin, Milk Road analyst, agreed but said CoreWeave and Nebius will be the top survivors.

"The majority of neocloud companies will NOT survive. I strongly believe we're going to see a MASSIVE amount of consolidation across this industry over the next several years, and only a handful of companies will come out on top," Melvin said.

"Personally, I think $CRWV and $NBIS will be the top 2," he said.

Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang, whose company is CoreWeave's second-largest investor with an approximately 10% stake, sought to reassure investors about its financial position.

"CoreWeave’s financial strength is improving every day," Huang told reporters at an event in Stockholm, adding that he did not see a need for Nvidia to backstop the company.

"I'm optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing."

Analysts see buying opportunity

Cantor Fitzgerald reiterated its Overweight rating on CoreWeave, with a $176 price target implying upside of more than 150% from its reference price.

The firm said CoreWeave had public support from Nvidia and had sold nearly all the capacity scheduled to come online in 2027.

Nvidia has an agreement to backstop any unsold capacity.

According to Cantor Fitzgerald, the principal concern is whether CoreWeave can finance the capital expenditure required to meet demand, rather than whether demand for AI computing exists.

The firm described the current period as an attractive opportunity to add to or initiate a position in the shares.

Deutsche Bank also maintained its Buy rating on CoreWeave, with a $150 price target, implying upside of more than 100% from its reference price.

Analyst Brad Zelnick acknowledged that the company's prospects are closely tied to the performance of the AI sector and demand for computing infrastructure.

He argued, however, that its underlying contracts provide meaningful support.

“The vast majority of CoreWeave’s backlog is associated with long-term take-or-pay contracts where contracted revenue fully covers all capital and operating costs associated with the contract and generates a return for the company,” Zelnick wrote.

He estimated that 60% to 65% of CoreWeave's backlog was tied to investment-grade customers at the end of the second quarter.

The company has used these contracts to secure project-specific debt at costs at or below its parent company's borrowing rate.

“A strong customer base, established record of execution, backlog conversion and leading infrastructure performance is all supportive of their issuer profile relative to neocloud peers, in our view,” Zelnick said.

Deutsche Bank also highlighted CoreWeave's financing arrangements and liquidity position.

“Available liquidity stood at $15.5 billion, and since that time the company: closed a $2.6 billion DDTL 5.5 (backed by shorter 3-yr contracts) at SOFR + 5.50%; closed a $4.2 billion 2.875% Convertible Senior Note and announced a 35 million share ATM equity program,” the bank said.

Capital needs remain a key risk

Despite the positive assessment of its customer contracts, CoreWeave faces substantial funding requirements as it expands its infrastructure.

Deutsche Bank forecasts operating cash flow of about $10 billion over the next 12 months, compared with required capital expenditure of roughly $45 billion.

That gap means the company will need to secure additional funding, although Zelnick argued it could raise capital at a steady pace, supported by its contracted customer backlog.

The central question for investors is whether CoreWeave can convert its substantial order book into cash flow quickly enough to support its expansion without putting further pressure on its balance sheet.

For now, bullish analysts see long-term contracts, investment-grade customers and Nvidia's support as reasons to look beyond the recent sell-off.

More cautious investors remain focused on the cost of financing the infrastructure boom and the risks of relying on future demand to justify heavy borrowing.
